analysis:
The only changed content in docs/architecture/inference.md is a documentation-only addition at head lines ~956-991. It describes an excluded startup shape warmup (ModelCalibrationPolicy.shapeWarmup) that runs once per loaded EngineV2 engine. Neither supplied unit (head lines 1-797) covers the changed range; the patch excerpt is truncated at the last visible sentence, so I could not see the remainder of the new section.

Reviewed security-relevant behavior from the visible text. The warmup uses a synthetic greedy 128-token probe and synthetic shape prompts. It trains no rates or counters and has a 20 s wall budget. It uses the artifact's default sampling and does not appear to touch consumer prompts, A-001, the prefix-cache SSD tier (T-041), keys, attestation or the coordinator wire. Because it is a documented warmup rather than serving, it does not alter TB-002, TB-007 or TB-011 authorization.

Open integration questions (unverified, not findings):
(1) Whether warmup submissions populate or donate to the encrypted SSD prefix cache (T-041). The warmup prompts would be synthetic and should be in a non-tenant scope. The visible text does not say whether they use a cacheSalt or skip donation.
(2) Whether warmup timing could be observed as a TTFT oracle. This appears not to be the case, since the scope is process-local.
(3) The 20 s warmup delay against the availability of provider connection control (T-057). It is bounded by the budget.

The remaining visible content (Nemotron Super and GLM5Next descriptions) is unchanged context. No code changes are supplied, so I identified no regression. The implementation in the referenced sources would need review to confirm that warmup requests do not bypass admission or leak into cache scopes.
